question.text: A vessel contains <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>14</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of nitrogen gas at a temperature of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>27</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>. The amount of heat to be transferred to the gas to double the r.m.s. speed of its molecules will be : (Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>32</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
The RMS speed of a gas at a given temperature is given by, vrms=3RTM.

Therefore, to double the RMS speed, the temperature should be increased to four times the initial temperature. Therefore,

Tf=1200 K, Ti=300 K, and n=1428=12

The volume of the vessel will remain the same therefore, the process is an isochoric process. Therefore,

Q=nCvΔT=12×5R2×900

⇒Q=9360 J
